title: Why Heavy Iron Ships Don't Sink 🚢
description: Massive ships made of solid iron weighing thousands of tons, but why don't they sink in water? Discover the scientific secret in one minute.

scenes.text: Iron ships weigh thousands of tons!
scenes.say: How does a massive iron ship weighing thousands of tons float on water, while a tiny piece of iron sinks?
Iron material is much heavier than water, which means the material alone should sink completely.
The secret lies in the hollow, air-filled design of the ship, which changes its overall density.
When we make the iron hollow, the average density becomes less than water, so the water pushes the ship upward.
The ship displaces a massive volume of water, creating an upward buoyant force that equals the entire weight of the ship.
